text: {"score":2,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the tools, and the next steps are reasonable. But the summary contradicts itself and misrepresents the chart evidence. The headline says 'charts support billing (1/30 below)', yet the only documented 99215 claim (1 of 1) was below the billed level. The rationale says 'Documentation in the complete random sample supports the codes. No finding.', which conflicts with the 100% below-billed statement and with the next step calling the records 'too thin to judge'. The 'no finding' conclusion rests on 30 charts of which only 1 was a 99215, so it overstates what the sample shows about 99215 billing. The summary also does not address the 50 excess 99215 claims or the 5.5x ratio, and it gives no per-complexity breakdown. The cited examples are mostly low-complexity 99215 claims, which fit the 46% point. C0019149 is a good example, but it is the only one with documentation. 'Of 1 documented 99215 claims, 1 (100%)' is a statistically meaningless comparison against 0%. The leaning 'inconclusive' is cautious and acceptable, but the mixed messaging would confuse an investigator.","problems":["Headline claims charts support billing while the sole documented 99215 was below billed level","Rationale states 'documentation supports the codes. No finding' contradicting its own 1/1 below-billed statistic and the next step saying records are too thin","Overstates conclusions from 30 charts that contain only one 99215 claim","Presents 1 of 1 (100%) vs 0% as a comparison without noting the sample is meaningless","Omits excess 99215 count (50) and ratio 5.5x and complexity-tier breakdown","Two of three cited examples have no documentation, so they only support the complexity point"]}
